newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby union-Australia and New Zealand in joint Cup bid.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Australia and New Zealand in joint Cup bid.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand have launched a joint bid to host the rugby union World Cup in 2003.
Australia would stage the tournament final as the host union under the plan, announced by union officials.

"(The bid) shows the level of cooperation and friendship which exists between the two rugby union bodies which enables us to reach an understanding," the chairman of the Australian Rugby Union (ARU), Dick McGruther, said in a statement.

"The joint bid will be an impressive one given the credentials of the two countries, not just in rugby terms, but also in terms of the range of other attributes we bring to the table in commercial, marketing, broadcasting and organisation," McGruther said.
South Africa won the World Cup as hosts in 1995 and Wales will stage the event in 1999.
The joint Australia-New Zealand plan involves four pool groups, with two based in each country.
The quarter-finals and semi-finals would also be shared, with the third and fourth place playoff to be played in New Zealand.
If the bid is successful, the final is almost certain to be played at the 80,000 capacity Olympic Stadium, now under construction at Homebush in Sydney.

"With Sydney hosting the 2000 Olympic Games, and given the magnificent facilities and infrastructure that will remain thereafter, for Sydney to host the rugby union World Cup in 2003 is a wonderful follow up," the ARU said.
Tenders must be submitted by September 30 before a final decision is made in January 1998, the ARU said.
